relflow turns a data schema into a trainable PyTorch model.
Describe the values you have and the outcome you want to predict.

For example, learn whether a payment will later be disputed:

```yaml
amount: 84.50
merchant: North Market
disputed: false
```

The model reads `amount` and `merchant`, and learns to predict `disputed`.
Later, add an account's transaction history as a nested collection.

[Build your first model →](getting-started.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

## Start Small

1. [Your first model](getting-started.qmd): define fields, train, and predict.
2. [Add transaction history](tutorials/transaction-history.qmd): give each payment a collection of earlier transactions.
3. [Work with your data](guides/data-modules.qmd): use Arrow, Polars, or Parquet datasets.

## Go Further When You Need To

- [Training and checkpoints](guides/lightning.qmd): control fitting, validation, and saved models.
- [Model structure](core-concepts/model-tree.qmd): understand nested contexts and configure the architecture.
- [Account risk example](case-studies/customer-risk.qmd): combine several histories and prediction targets.

The examples use payments and accounts. The same field and branch definitions
work with other kinds of tabular and nested records.
